items.text: Fallen Swan
The farce has come to an end.
The sparse vegetation in her garden has been left in disarray by the incident. The purple potato flowers lie scattered upon the soil.

items.speaker: Grandma
items.text: Nice! It's spud season again.

items.speaker: Grandma
items.text: Charlotte, I've made ye mashed tatties for breakfast today, with plenty of sweet cream—yer favorite.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Coach says I can't eat this anymore. Floor Ritualists need to keep their figures trim. She says that if I want to win the gold, I need to—

items.speaker: Grandma
items.text: Oh, Charlotte. Now they've got ye worried about yer eating too?

items.speaker: Grandma
items.text: I know you're a good little thing, and you like yer Floor Ritual very much, but with all that training ye do, and with all this growing you've still to do, you have to eat properly, otherwise you'll wither away into nothing!

items.speaker: Grandma
items.text: Just take one bite, eh? How about it?

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: One bite ...

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: What did you have for breakfast?
Her eyes are fixed on the small clump of mashed potatoes left hanging on the girl's chest.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Creamy mashed potatoes?
Before the girl can react, she explodes.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: How many times have I told you?! If you want results, you can't eat rubbish like this!

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I was just trying to get a little energy.
They both know this is just an excuse.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: The Uluru qualifiers are in three days, Charlotte! Did you forget that little fact?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Or do you think that pathetic speck of talent of yours gives you the right to get complacent? Eh?!

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: If that's what you think, then let me tell you now, Charlotte.
A cruel smile spreads across her face.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: What a waste of space you are.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: There'll be no shortage of talent at the qualifiers.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Why? I know I shouldn't have done it, but you don't need to humiliate me like this!

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Humiliate you?
She gives a sharp, cruel laugh.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: You're right. I don't need to humiliate you. Because the moment you walk out on that floor beside real athletes, you'll have already done it to yourself.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Go ahead. I won't stop you.
She is casual in the face of this cruel remark.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Go ahead and eat your creamy mashed potatoes if you love them so much. Oh, and Her Majesty needs her beauty sleep, too. Why not go ahead and cancel your morning training? In fact, why not take the whole day off?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Sports are just too exhausting, I know. Not only do you have to put up with your aching muscles, but you have to watch what you eat and deal with your bossy old coach. After all, you're Lady Charlotte, a fine noblewoman.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: How could a noble be asked to sweat on the red land of Uluru? She should be sitting in the audience, yes, in the audience with a parasol and a cool drink, no?

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: I shan't waste my energy on you any longer.
She turns and exits the training ground without a backward glance.
Charlotte slowly clenches her fists.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Feck!

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I'm not ...
She punches the wall, and the pain in her knuckles fills her with bitterness.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I am not Lady Charlotte!!
She grits her teeth as her sinuses sting. She holds back her emotions, not letting the tears flow from her eyes.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I will win that gold medal.
She presses her leg hard against the wall, her whole body bending into a gentle curve.
She begins the routine she has practiced a thousand times before, but this time alone in the room. Her body traces arcs in the air as she leaps and lands through each element.
She silently records the score of each element as she goes.
Next comes the most important part—the arcane skill segment.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Huff ... huff ...
She closes her eyes.
Invisible energy flows through the air.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Phew. Eye of Day, Keeper of Balance. You are the Endless Well.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Healing Sulis, shining Sulis, holy Sulis, to us, you tell.
A faint glow appears before her eyes.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: You warm our souls, heal our wounds, and grant us endless peace.
The light is as warm as spring. She reaches out her hand to it.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: If only I could touch the hem of your garment, that flowing, loving radiance ...

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Did I do something wrong? Why can't I see your radiance?
The energy still flows beside her, stirring her hair and softly ruffling the feathers on her leotard.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Why can't I see you? Why do you reject me? How can I win your favor?
In the endless darkness, her voice is the only echo.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I'll do anything—give you anything—just please, let me win that gold medal!

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Hah.
That voice shouldn't be here. She opens her eyes, startled.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: What are you—

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: I came to get the wire recorder.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: The wire recorder?
But the wire recorder is for everyone to use. It's always in the training room. She's never seen anyone take it out of here before.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Charlotte, the cruelty of competitive sports is that even if you give everything, you're very likely to end up with nothing in return.
She continues, half speaking to herself.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: I thought you'd understand this. But, no, you're just a ridiculous, foolish little girl.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Think about those who came before you. Saoirse, for example. Everyone thought she'd win the games hands down, even her competitors.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: But in the end, she injured herself before she could compete. She never even saw Uluru for herself, only heard those three haunting syllables repeated by everyone around her. Of course, you know better than I what happened to her after that.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: She jumped off London Bridge.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: What makes you think you won't be the next? That you won't end up like her?

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I—

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: On your feet!
An unexpected command.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: The last element you just performed. Do it again.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: The qualifiers are just around the corner, and you're still jumping like that? If you aren't able to bring forth your arcane skill, you absolutely cannot afford to make a single mistake in the rest of your routine.
